method: Bounded source-only review; no engine invocation or allocator measurement.

finding.allocation: Builds an unordered_map<Id,vector<size_t>> index for every relation row on the first lookup for a column.
finding.admissionGap: The map nodes, buckets and per-key vector capacities have no query-owned byte budget. Core::evaluate builds the index before candidate matching is charged.

relatedLocations.role: Candidate work charging occurs only after index selection.
Dictionary units count reverse Entry and string bytes, excluding hash-map nodes, bucket capacities and relation indexes.

concreteCase.shape: One distinct entity and integer per active n-attribute fact; remaining retained facts outside attribute scope.
concreteCase.expectedSourceBehavior: Full entity-column index is allocated before finding no matching entity. The empty answer may use zero candidate work. This behavior was inferred from source and has not been measured.
concreteCase.concurrency: Sixteen independent readers can each own such evaluator/index allocations.

scope: Native evaluator input remains capped at100000; this is not a claim of million-row native evaluation.
Existing work accounting intentionally models candidate scans. The finding concerns physical allocation coverage, not changed query semantics.
Scalable SQL does not execute this Core. It retains its separate logical row/carrier admission and DuckDB buffer/spill controls.
No aggregate process-memory cap or allocator envelope is established by this review.

proposedRegression.fixture: Build admitted unique-entity n facts through native commands, with an absent entity literal and maxWork1.
proposedRegression.instrumentation: Introduce query-owned counting allocation/high-water accounting for Core relation/index/dictionary containers before asserting a physical budget.
assertions: A small explicit native-heap budget rejects before constructing the full oversized index.
The error returns no partial answer and a subsequent small query on the same store succeeds.
A sufficient budget returns the same empty typed set and reports a nonzero index-allocation high-water.
A sixteen-reader run records per-invocation and total high-waters separately from sampled RSS.
proposedRegression.implementationCandidate: A bounded allocator or PMR resource covering map nodes, bucket arrays and vectors; keep existing logical fact/work semantics unless explicitly changed.
